title: Development and Testing of a Synthetic Skin Microbial Community
author: Thiruppathy, Lekbua, et al.
materials: Timing: ∼variable (depends on extraction protocols and capabilities)

DNA extraction from all communities constructed is performed using the Qiagen DNeasy PowerSoil Pro Kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions using community pellets. The protocol involves 5 key steps - lysis (chemical and mechanical), inhibitor removal, DNA binding, washing, and elution.20.For sample lysis, transfer the contents from each well in the target plate to a fresh Eppendorf tube (1.5 mL).21.Spin down the samples at 10,000 g for 2 min and discard the supernatant.Note: Include transfer of the content from the negative control wells to account for contaminating microbial DNA during sample prep.1322.Resuspend the pellet in 800 μL of CD1 solution provided in the kit. Pipette mix briefly or vortex.23.Transfer the entire contents to a PowerBead Pro tube provided in the kit.24.Perform mechanical lysis in tandem with chemical lysis (CD1 solution) by securing the PowerBead pro tubes to a Vortex Adapter horizontally. Vortex at max speed for 12 min.25.Follow the manufacturer’s instructions until pure, inhibitor free DNA is eluted, which can be verified using Qubit (Invitrogen), NanoDrop (Thermo Scientific), or even a BioAnalyzer (Tape Station) (Agilent).Note: DNA can be eluted using RNAse-free water instead of C6 solution.26.Quantify the concentration of DNA extracted using the Qubit HS DNA assay.Note: Ensure the Qubit has been calibrated using manufacturer provided standards.Pause Point: DNA can be stored at −20 C indefinitely after this step, however, avoid frequent freeze-thawing cycles.

steps.title: Prepare consumables and resources
steps.instruction: Label and date all microbial consumables, select candidate skin microbes that grow on the same basal media, house all mice in the same room with controlled light/dark cycles, temperature and humidity, and install the required R version and packages.

steps.title: Normalize bacterial pre‑cultures
steps.instruction: Grow each bacterial strain to fresh pre‑culture and adjust the optical density to OD600 = 0.07 before use.

steps.title: Set up CellenONE X1 and load plates
steps.instruction: Prime the CellenONE X1, load the probe and target plates, and run the community construction program.

substeps.instruction: Prime the CellenONE X1 as described in the system‑validation section.
Fill the probe plate with the OD600‑0.07 bacterial suspensions.
Add 200 µL of 1X BHI to each well of the target plate.
Insert the probe and target plates into their designated slots.
Load the community‑construction field file (Supplementary Data) and execute the Setup Target steps (steps 8‑10).
Run the community‑construction program (≈6 h total assembly time).

steps.title: Incubate assembled community
steps.instruction: Cover, humidify and incubate the assembled plate, then monitor growth spectrophotometrically for 96 h.

substeps.instruction: Cover the target plate with an anti‑condensation coated lid.
Place the plate in a 37 °C incubator.
Create a local humidified environment by stacking the plate on four petri dishes filled with water.
Take regular absorbance readings of each well with a spectrophotometer for the next 96 h (≈3 days).
Verify reproducibility and stability with at least four independent replicates.

steps.title: Extract DNA with PowerSoil Pro
steps.instruction: Lyse cells, remove inhibitors, bind, wash and elute DNA from each well using the Qiagen DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the entire contents of each target‑plate well (including negative‑control wells) to a fresh 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Spin the tubes at 10 000 g for 2 min and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend each pellet in 800 µL of CD1 solution (provided with the kit) and vortex briefly.
Transfer the suspension to a PowerBead Pro tube.
Secure the tube in a vortex adapter and vortex at maximum speed for 12 min to achieve combined chemical and mechanical lysis.
Continue with the kit’s inhibitor‑removal, DNA‑binding, washing and elution steps as instructed by the manufacturer (DNA may be eluted in RNase‑free water instead of C6 solution).
Quantify the eluted DNA with the Qubit HS DNA assay (calibrated with the supplied standards).
Store extracted DNA at –20 °C indefinitely; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles.

steps.title: Prepare Nextera‑XT sequencing libraries
steps.instruction: Tagment, index, amplify, clean, quantify, normalize and pool libraries for NovaSeq sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 5 µL of each DNA sample (0.5 ng/µL) to a new tube for tagmentation.
Add the manufacturer‑specified volumes of Amplicon Tagment Mix (ATM) and Tagment DNA Buffer (TD).
Add 5 µL of extracted control DNA to each reaction (to monitor reagent contamination).
Optionally include 5 µL of a ZymoBIOMICS Microbial Community Standard as a positive control.
Incubate the tagmentation mix at 55 °C for 10 min.
Cool the reaction to 10 °C and immediately add the recommended amount of Neutralize Tagment Buffer (NT) to stop the reaction.
Add 10 µL of Nextera‑XT Index Kit v.2 indices (dual‑index barcoding) to each sample; ensure each sample receives a unique index combination.
Amplify the indexed libraries for 12 PCR cycles (alternatively, use 9 µL index + 1 µL 1× SYBR Green for qPCR‑based monitoring).
Perform post‑amplification cleanup according to the kit protocol.
Quantify the cleaned libraries with the Qubit HS DNA assay (calibrated with standards).
Normalize each library to a final concentration of 10 nM.
Pool normalized libraries, combining no more than 150 samples per NovaSeq lane to guarantee ≥5 million reads per sample.
Store pooled libraries at –20 °C indefinitely.
Ship the pooled libraries for paired‑end 150 bp sequencing on an Illumina NovaSeq 6000, requesting a 5 % PhiX spike‑in and a minimum of 5 million reads per sample.

steps.title: Install Conda environment for analysis
steps.instruction: Download and install Miniconda, then create a dedicated environment with all required bioinformatics tools.

substeps.instruction: Create a directory and download the Miniconda installer:
mkdir ~/miniconda3
wget https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh -O ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh
Run the installer in batch mode:
bash ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh -b -u -p ~/miniconda3
Optionally delete the installer script:
rm ~/miniconda3/miniconda.sh
Create a new Conda environment and install required packages:
conda create -n metagenomics_pipeline -c bioconda trim-galore bowtie2 woltka python=3.8
Activate the environment:
conda activate metagenomics_pipeline

steps.title: Build Bowtie2 index for SkinCom references
steps.instruction: Generate a Bowtie2 index from the SkinCom reference FASTA file.

substeps.instruction: Place all SkinCom genome sequences in a single FASTA file (one header per species).
Run:
bowtie2-build --threads <NUM_THREADS> skincom_reference.fasta ./skincom_index/skincom
The index files will be created in ./skincom_index/ with the prefix “skincom”.

steps.title: Trim and concatenate raw reads
steps.instruction: Perform adapter and quality trimming, then merge R1 and R2 files for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Run Trim Galore on paired‑end reads:
trim_galore --paired --quality 20 --fastqc -o trimmed_reads/ sample_R1.fastq.gz sample_R2.fastq.gz
Concatenate the trimmed R1 and R2 files:
cat *R1*trimmed*.fq.gz *R2*trimmed*.fq.gz > _trimmed.fq.gz

steps.title: Create alignment output directories
steps.instruction: Make folders to store SAM and Bowtie2 statistics files.

substeps.instruction: mkdir -p ~/aligned/samfiles
mkdir -p ~/aligned/bowfiles

steps.title: Align reads with Bowtie2
steps.instruction: Map the trimmed reads to the SkinCom index and capture alignment statistics.

substeps.instruction: bowtie2 -U _trimmed.fq.gz -x ./skincom_index/skincom -p <NUM_THREADS> -S ~/aligned/samfiles/sample.sam 2> ~/aligned/bowfiles/sample.bow
Optional: add --no-header and --no-unal to reduce SAM file size if storage is limited.

steps.title: Classify reads with woltka
steps.instruction: Generate a taxon count table from the SAM files.

substeps.instruction: woltka classify -i ~/aligned/samfiles -o ~/taxons.tsv

steps.title: Deactivate Conda environment
steps.instruction: Exit the analysis environment after all commands have completed.

description: 1.Clearly label and date all consumables containing microbes.2.Choose candidate microbes for the synthetic microbial community. The selected candidates should be abundant in the human skin microbiome characterized across multiple studies and represent the biome’s metabolic diversity (aerobic, microaerophilic, and anaerobic organisms; gram-positive and gram-negative). They must also grow on the same basal media mix.3.Ensure all mice are housed in the same experimental room with the appropriate light/dark cycles and controlled for temperature and humidity.4.Ensure you have access to the appropriate versions of R and corresponding packages (see key resources table for full list of packages and the required versions).
